findings.title: TCP Handshake Enforcement Disabled
findings.description: TCP handshake enforcement is disabled.
findings.business_impact: Out-of-state TCP packets may be forwarded, aiding evasion.
findings.technical_impact: Firewall does not require a full handshake before forwarding.
findings.remediation: Enable TCP handshake enforcement under Firewall Settings > Flood Protection.
verification: Confirm TCP handshake enforcement is enabled

findings.title: HA control-link encryption disabled
findings.description: State synchronisation between HA peers is not encrypted.
findings.business_impact: Session/state data on the HA link is readable by anyone with access to that segment.
findings.technical_impact: HA sync traffic, including connection state, transits in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Enable HA encryption, or guarantee the HA link is a dedicated, physically secured point-to-point connection.
verification: Confirm 'Enable Encryption: Yes' under HA settings

findings.title: Default 'admin' account name in use
findings.description: The built-in administrator account retains the default name 'admin'.
findings.business_impact: Attackers can skip username enumeration; brute-force tooling targets 'admin' by default.
findings.technical_impact: Halves the effort of credential attacks against the management plane.
findings.remediation: Rename the built-in administrator account to a non-obvious value and document it in your password vault.
verification: Confirm login with the old 'admin' name fails
findings.risk_reduction: Low - removes a free hint for attackers.

findings.title: SonicOS API accepts MD5 digest authentication
findings.description: The SonicOS API has RFC-7616 digest authentication enabled with the MD5 algorithm permitted.
findings.business_impact: API authentication can be downgraded to a cryptographically broken hash, weakening automation credentials.
findings.technical_impact: MD5 digests are vulnerable to collision and accelerated brute-force attacks.
findings.remediation: Disable the MD5 digest algorithm for the SonicOS API, leaving SHA-256 only. Prefer token-based (Bearer) authentication for automation.
verification: Confirm 'MD5: No' under enabled digest algorithms
findings.risk_reduction: Low - removes a weak-crypto authentication path.

findings.title: Enhanced audit logging disabled
findings.description: Enhanced audit logging of configuration changes is disabled.
findings.business_impact: Configuration changes lack a detailed audit trail, complicating incident response and change accountability.
findings.technical_impact: Per-parameter change attribution is unavailable during forensics.
findings.remediation: Enable Enhanced Audit Logging and forward events to the central log platform.
verification: Make a benign change and confirm an audit event is produced

findings.title: Gateway Anti-Virus HTTP outbound inspection disabled

findings.remediation: Enable HTTP outbound inspection in Gateway Anti-Virus settings.

matched_advisories.title: SonicOS affected by multiple vulnerabilities (auth bypass, path traversal, DoS)
matched_advisories.summary: Improper access control (CVE-2026-0204, CVSS 8.0, CWE-1390/306) may allow an unauthenticated attacker on an adjacent network to reach management-interface functions without authentication; combined with a post-auth path traversal (CVE-2026-0205, CVSS 6.8) and a post-auth stack-based buffer overflow DoS (CVE-2026-0206). Affects Gen6/Gen7/Gen8.
matched_advisories.upgrade_recommendation: Upgrade to 7.3.1-7014 or later to remediate CVE-2026-0204, CVE-2026-0205, CVE-2026-0206.

matched_advisories.title: SonicOS SSLVPN Pre-Auth Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability
matched_advisories.summary: A pre-authentication stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) in the SonicOS SSLVPN service lets a remote unauthenticated attacker crash the firewall, causing denial of service. Only devices with the SSLVPN interface/service enabled are exposed.
matched_advisories.upgrade_recommendation: Upgrade to 7.3.1-7013 or later to remediate CVE-2025-40601.

attack_paths.name: Internet-facing management-plane compromise

stages.detail: Attacker scans the WAN IP and finds the firewall management service exposed (FW-MGT-001).
A firmware advisory (max CVSS 8.0) is applicable to the running build, providing a remote exploitation primitive.
Weak password policy and/or absent MFA on the admin account lowers the bar for authentication bypass or brute force (FW-MGT-003/FW-MGT-004).
Administrative control of the firewall enables rule changes, traffic interception, and pivoting into protected zones.

attack_paths.narrative: An internet-based attacker discovers the exposed management interface, leverages an applicable firmware vulnerability, exploits weak or single-factor authentication, and gains administrative control of the firewall.

attack_paths.name: SSL VPN foothold escalating to firewall management

stages.detail: Attacker targets the WAN-exposed SSL VPN portal with credential stuffing or post-disclosure exploitation (FW-SSL-001).
Web management is reachable over SSL VPN, so a valid VPN session reaches the firewall admin UI (FW-SSL-003).
No admin MFA means a single captured/guessed credential completes the takeover (FW-MGT-004).
Administrative access to the firewall from a remote-access foothold.

attack_paths.narrative: An attacker compromises an SSL VPN credential, reaches the firewall web management interface that is exposed over the VPN, and escalates to administrative control because the admin account lacks MFA.

attack_paths.name: Encrypted-traffic inspection blind spot

stages.detail: Malware is delivered inside a TLS session; with DPI-SSL off the firewall cannot inspect the payload (FW-SVC-001).
Reduced or disabled inline services widen the gap for the payload to reach the host uninspected.
Encrypted C2 leaves the network unseen, enabling persistence and data exfiltration.

attack_paths.narrative: Because encrypted traffic is not inspected and one or more inline engines are reduced, malware delivery and command-and-control over TLS pass through the firewall undetected.
